response.goal: Fix the n8n workflow so the full file of about 5,000 rows lands every night in Google Sheets without failing due to rate limits, with retries and a Slack message if it still fails.

plan.step: Audit the existing n8n workflow and analyze the Google Sheets node configuration handling the 5,000 CSV rows.
Implement batching or rate-limit handling to prevent the 429 Too Many Requests error when appending rows to Google Sheets.
Configure error handling with retries in the n8n workflow for the Google Sheets import.
Add a Slack notification node to alert the team if the workflow fails after retries.

milestones.name: Audit and Fix
milestones.deliverable: Updated n8n workflow with batching and rate-limit handling for Google Sheets.

milestones.name: Error Handling and Testing
milestones.deliverable: Configured retries and Slack failure alerts, verified with a full test run.

risks.risk: Google Sheets API write quotas may still be exceeded if batch sizes are not optimized.
risks.mitigation: Split the 5,000 rows into smaller chunks with appropriate delays between batches.

risks.risk: Lack of access to the existing n8n instance or Google Sheet.
risks.mitigation: Request temporary workspace access or export of the workflow JSON before starting.

questions: Can we access your n8n instance and Google Sheet to review the current workflow setup?
What is the exact structure and size of the CSV file imported each night?
assumptions: The client will provide necessary credentials and access to the n8n instance and Google Sheets.
